newsitem.title: USA: Four crossing the Atlantic in inflatable boat.
newsitem.headline: Four crossing the Atlantic in inflatable boat.

text.p: Four Britons set out on Sunday from Portsmouth, New Hampshire, in a 24-foot (6-metre) inflatable boat to see if they could motor across the Atlantic to Portsmouth, England.
"We looked around for the next big thrill, and the might of the Atlantic was the crew's choice," Alan Priddy, 43, said in a prepared statement.

Priddy, Vic Palmer, 52, Steve Lloyd, 44, and Jan Falkowski, 36, have dedicated their 4,100-mile (6,598-km) voyage, which will take them north to Nova Scotia, then to Labrador, Greenland, Iceland and Northern Ireland before reaching Portsmouth, to the Cancer Care Society, a British charity.
The rigid inflatable boat was shipped from England, but on the way its navigation equipment was stolen.

Raytheon Co, the Lexington, Massachusetts-based defense giant that makes navigation equipment, donated a radar system for the trip through waters known for dense fog, drifting icebergs and subfreezing temperatures.
The journey is expected to take 13 to 14 days and raise $160,000 for cancer research.
